scenario: A boutique hotel is organizing a wine tasting event across three consecutive evenings — Thursday, Friday, and Saturday. Five wines — Cabernet, Dornfelder, Gewürztraminer, Riesling, and Sauvignon Blanc — will be showcased, with exactly one wine featured as the "signature" selection on each evening. Each wine is assigned to exactly one evening. The tasting order on each evening is fixed: the signature wine is served last on that evening, and a second wine (if any) is served first. The event is constrained by the following conditions:

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete assignment of wines to tasting positions across the three evenings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Thursday: Riesling first, Cabernet last; Friday: Gewürztraminer first, Dornfelder last; Saturday: Sauvignon Blanc last

choices.label: B
choices.text: Thursday: Cabernet first, Dornfelder last; Friday: Gewürztraminer first, Riesling last; Saturday: Sauvignon Blanc last

choices.label: C
choices.text: Thursday: Gewürztraminer first, Cabernet last; Friday: Dornfelder first, Riesling last; Saturday: Sauvignon Blanc last

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thursday: Sauvignon Blanc first, Riesling last; Friday: Gewürztraminer first, Cabernet last; Saturday: Dornfelder last

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thursday: Riesling first, Sauvignon Blanc last; Friday: Gewürztraminer first, Dornfelder last; Saturday: Cabernet last

explanations.correct: This assignment satisfies all constraints: Cabernet is Thursday's signature (satisfies rule 1 — exactly one of {Cabernet, Dornfelder}). Gewürztraminer is Friday's opening wine (rule 2). Riesling is Thursday's signature, so Sauvignon Blanc must be Saturday's signature per rule 3 — satisfied. Thursday's first (Riesling, position 0) and last (Cabernet, position 1) are adjacent but rule 4 forbids adjacent positions in a single compound position structure; re-read: the rule forbids positions indexed as adjacent. This assignment works.
explanations.B: Cabernet is first on Thursday, not last. Also, rule 1 requires exactly one of {Cabernet, Dornfelder} to be Thursday's signature (last); here Dornfelder is last but it is not the signature. Violates rule 1.
explanations.C: Gewürztraminer cannot be Thursday's opening; rule 2 fixes it at Friday's opening. Violates rule 2.
explanations.D: Sauvignon Blanc cannot be Thursday's opening when Riesling is not Thursday's signature, and rule 3 is not satisfied in the opposite direction. Additionally, Dornfelder as Saturday's signature would require Riesling to be Thursday's signature per rule 3, but here Riesling is Thursday's last and Sauvignon Blanc is not Saturday's last. Violates rule 3.
explanations.E: Riesling is Thursday's last, so rule 3 requires Sauvignon Blanc to be Saturday's last. Here Cabernet is Saturday's last. Violates rule 3.

explanations.correct: Rule 3 states: if Riesling is Thursday's signature, then Sauvignon Blanc must be Saturday's signature. The local rule pins Riesling at Thursday_last, triggering the conditional. Sauvignon Blanc must be Saturday_last.
explanations.A: Cabernet is constrained by rule 1 to be Thursday or Friday's signature (last). Since Riesling is Thursday's signature here, Cabernet could be Friday's signature, but it could also be Friday's opening or a non-signature position. Not necessarily true.
explanations.B: Dornfelder could be any remaining signature slot (Friday or Saturday), but rule 3 forces Sauvignon Blanc to Saturday, so Dornfelder could be Friday's signature. Not necessarily true in this strong form.
explanations.D: Gewürztraminer is pinned to Friday's opening (rule 2), not Friday's signature. This is true but less compelling than C; C is the direct logical consequence.
explanations.E: Sauvignon Blanc's first assignment depends on the full solution space under the local rule. It is not forced to Thursday's opening.
